description: §15.11.4 + §42.3.5 (S459 round 7) — every absence-safe form of calling an OPTIONAL function prop compiles (no E-TYPE-031) and runs, for an instance that omits the prop (#none: nothing happens, nothing throws; the `if=`-guarded buttons are not rendered) and one that passes it (#some: each form calls it once — 11 calls): optional call `onGo?.()`; `if=onGo` on the element and on an ancestor; early return on `onGo is not` / `!onGo` / `onGo == not`; `is some` consequent; truthy consequent; else of a negated test; ternary consequent; `&&` right operand. The judgement is the one §42 presence-narrowing reader (presence-narrowing.ts) E-TYPE-046 uses for a `T | not` cell. Round 6 refused six of these.
rationale: §42.3.5: absence-safe = "Optional chaining the access itself — … `recv?.method(...)`" or "Narrowing … via any canonical presence-discrimination: the `if=` markup guard (§42.4), `given recv :> { ... }`, an `if (recv is not) return` / `is some` early-return, or a `match recv …` arm". §15.11.4 requires "an absence check" before calling an optional function prop.
